slides.title: Selection and distribution
slides.main: A multiplexer selects, a demultiplexer distributes, a decoder turns a number into a line.

captions: A multiplexer chooses one of several inputs and passes it to the output
A demultiplexer directs one input to the chosen output
A decoder lights a line by number, an encoder finds the number by the line

slides.title: Multiplexer 2→1
slides.main: Y = not S · A + S · B — two ANDs, one OR and an inverter.

captions: Selector is zero — A goes to the output
Selector is one — B goes to the output
Not S · A + S · B: two AND gates, one OR and an inverter

frames.text: Y = not S · A + S · B

slides.title: Enable and controllable inverter
slides.main: The enable input switches a block off, and a multiplexer with B and not B gives XOR.

captions: While enable is zero, the output stays silent whatever the multiplexer chose
At one the circuit works as an ordinary multiplexer
Feed B and its negation, selector A: at A = 0 the signal B passes as is
At A = 1 the signal B is inverted — we got exclusive OR

slides.title: Multiplexer 4→1
slides.main: The number of gates grows linearly, the depth as the logarithm of the inputs.

captions: Two first-level multiplexers choose within pairs by the low bit S0
The second-level multiplexer chooses between the pairs by the high bit S1
Eight-to-one and sixteen-to-one are built the same way — just add levels
The number of gates grows linearly, and the circuit depth only logarithmically

slides.title: Bus multiplexer
slides.main: A bus is a group of wires: one select signal switches the whole word at once.

captions: A bus is a group of wires carrying a whole word; word A goes to the output
The same two bits are switched by one selector — now word B goes

frames.text: S: one signal for the whole word
S: one signal for the whole word

slides.title: Demultiplexer 1→2
slides.sub: One input to one of the outputs
slides.main: Y0 = A · not S, Y1 = A · S — two AND gates with a shared selector.

captions: Selector is zero: the signal goes to Y0, and Y1 stays zero
Selector is one: the signal goes to Y1, and Y0 stays zero
Two AND gates with shared input A and the selector in opposite polarity

slides.title: Decoder 2→4
slides.sub: A number becomes a lit line
slides.main: Decoders select a memory cell, a register and an instruction.

captions: Code 00 lights line zero: exactly one of four is lit
Code 01 — line one
Code 10 — line two; this is how a register is chosen by number or a memory cell by address
Code 11 — line three; each output is an AND gate of inputs in the right polarity

slides.title: Enable and 3→8
slides.main: The high address bit chooses which of the 2→4 decoders works.

captions: A decoder with enable is a 1→4 demultiplexer: data goes to the selected line
If the data is zero, no line is lit
A 3→8 is built from two 2→4 decoders: the high bit turns on the needed one

slides.title: Priority encoder
slides.main: Priority and the flag V decide what to do when several lines are lit, or none.

captions: Only I2 is lit — its number 10 is on the output
I3 and I1 are lit: the higher one wins, the output is 11
With no active inputs, code 00 is indistinguishable from line zero — hence the flag V

slides.title: Universality
slides.main: A multiplexer is a truth table in hardware; NOR is a universal gate.

captions: Feed the truth table to the data inputs, the variables to the selector: the multiplexer implements any function
The same multiplexer at A = 1, B = 1 picks the fourth input — we get zero
And the NOR gate itself is universal: it gives NOT, OR and AND

frames.text: A AND B = NOR(NOT A, NOT B)
